original_record.question:
A square bit of paper is folded along the dashed lines in some order and direction. One of the corners of the resulting small square is cut off. The piece of paper is then unfolded. How many holes are on the inner area of the piece of paper?
<image1>
original_record.subject: transformation geometry

inventory: Three stages: 3×3 square with four dashed folds, right arrow, small plain square, right arrow, same square with upper-right corner clipped. No options or extra labels.
audit.explicit_conditions: Question transformation and pictured connectivity, options, hole types/positions; no inferred metric labels.
audit.display_conditions: Uniform scale and panel arrangement only.

answer_review.reason: A corner of the folded thirds has one interior preimage in each coordinate; their Cartesian product gives exactly one fully interior cutout (other cutouts meet the boundary), hence 1.
